text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.9% today to $140.62, driven by a sharp jump in oil prices following Saudi Arabia's pipeline closure after a drone attack. U.S. crude topped $105 a barrel—well above today's closing price of $97.26, suggesting the market is pricing in near-term supply disruption. The Saudi energy minister said the outage would last only days, but analysts are flagging risk: if the pipeline stays offline longer than five to seven days, oil inventories could tighten significantly and prices could spike further.

Oil majors like ConocoPhillips benefit directly when crude prices rise, since they produce more barrels and sell them at higher prices. The jump also fits into a broader trend where oil prices and broader market yields are moving in lockstep—a seven-year correlation high that suggests geopolitical oil shocks are dominating market sentiment right now.
